items.name: VoiceStudio
items.description: Fully local ElevenLabs alternative: voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription, audiobooks; 646 languages; Electron app for Windows/macOS/Linux/Docker; local API + MCP server; powered by k2-fsa/OmniVoice
items.verdictNote: adopt
items.why: AGPL-3.0 covers the software, not generated audio; do not embed in a hosted paid service without source release Each speech model has its own licence; review before commercial use Shares the 8GB card with ComfyUI; queue audio and image jobs Clone only your own voice or with written permission

items.name: Image2Splat (unresolved)
items.description: Category: single-image 3D Gaussian splatting. Closest practical option is Apple Research LiTo via ComfyUI-LiTo (~524K splats per image, ~4.7s on H100, ~3GB checkpoint)
items.verdictNote: niche: product pages, not games
items.why: Splats are not game-ready: no mesh, rig, collision or animation; need a dedicated renderer; large files unsuitable for fast-loading web games For indie-game 3D assets, evaluate image-to-mesh models instead since Godot imports meshes directly 4060 will be far slower than the quoted H100 timing CORRECTION from the AnyAngle analysis: single-image 3D/splat does have a strong role as a THROWAWAY INTERMEDIATE - reconstruct, render a reference angle in Blender, discard the 3D. Never shipped to a viewer, so file size and lack of rig do not matter.

items.name: QI_2.1_AnyAngle (LoRA)
items.description: LoRA for Qwen-Image-2.1 that re-renders an existing subject from a new camera angle while preserving the original art style. NOT one-click: four-stage chain = image -> 3D (Trellis2 or Tripo Splat) -> Blender camera placement -> render -> Qwen-Image-2.1 + LoRA using that render as reference. Settings: LoRA strength 1.0, CFG 3.0, 20+ steps, prompt 'Change the camera angle from <image2> to <image1>.'
items.verdictNote: specialist tool for product imagery; add to library, do not restructure the pipeline
items.why: NOT a replacement or fallback for Flux - it does a different job; Flux generates from a prompt, this re-angles an existing subject Base model Qwen-Image-2.1 needs ~16GB VRAM vs the 4060's 8GB; GGUF quants exist but quality drops and generation falls to minutes per image Trellis2 step needs its own VRAM; card already shared with Flux and VoiceStudio Blender camera placement is human judgement - does not automate cleanly Degrades when the 3D reconstruction is deformed; faces and low-res inputs worst affected Small community LoRA (71 likes), not a major release Cheaper answers first: for a game model once in Blender and render N views (free, perfectly consistent); for flat art generate a multi-view character sheet in ONE Flux pass

items.name: Supertonic 3
items.description: ~99M-parameter on-device TTS via ONNX Runtime. 31 languages, 44.1kHz 16-bit output, CPU-only (no CUDA/MPS upstream), RTF ~0.3x on a Raspberry Pi. Bindings: Python, Node.js, browser/WebGPU, Java, C++, C#, Go, Swift, iOS, Rust, Flutter. ALREADY SHIPS AS A VOICESTUDIO ENGINE: enable with 'uv sync --extra supertonic' or the in-app Model Catalogue, then accept the OpenRAIL-M licence in-app. Runs as a separate process so a crash cannot block other VoiceStudio features. Seven preset voices: M1 (default), M3, M4, M5, F3, F4, F5.
items.verdictNote: adopt as a SECOND engine inside VoiceStudio - one command, no new vendor; closes the voice-fallback gap
items.why: NOT a replacement for VoiceStudio's default engine: 'No cloning and no voice design - preset voices only' (VoiceStudio docs) Custom voices require Supertone's separate Voice Builder service, which breaks the fully-local property finance-education brand voice must stay on VoiceStudio's default engine (local GPU) Model is OpenRAIL-M: use-based restrictions (impersonation, deception); VoiceStudio docs note it 'restricts commercial use compared to VoiceStudio's standard terms' - read Attachment A before shipping a paid product CPU-only by design upstream; no hardware acceleration available ESP32-S3 is out of reach - 99M params needs real RAM; this is the Raspberry Pi tier, not the microcontroller tier MAINTENANCE FLAG: repo surfaces under both supertone-inc and supertone-oss-archive paths, suggesting a move to an archive org; reaching it via VoiceStudio's engine layer insulates you somewhat

items.name: ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context
items.description: ComfyUI node pack that chains MiniMax H3 clips with motion AND audio continuity: feeds previous clip's tail frames (5/22/39, 22 recommended) as context and remaps pinned audio onto the new clip's timeline; trim node removes the overlap. Local only, no API.
items.verdictNote: not adopted now; technique recorded. REVISIT when a 24 GB GPU is available. Owner decision (2026-10-03): keep the small-chunk, clip-by-clip workflow because each clip can be re-edited on its own instead of re-rendering one long take; single long takes are only worth it once hardware can iterate on them cheaply.
items.why: Works ONLY with MiniMax H3 running locally; the plan uses H3 via API, so the node does nothing for you Local H3 on 8GB is unverified per local-install guides; documented floor is a heavily offloaded 12GB card H3 open-weight licence excludes US/EU/UK/South Korea and reportedly restricts display outside its territory; Canada not excluded, but finance-education Shorts viewed mainly by US audiences may fall outside - read licence before publishing local H3 output 0 stars, last updated early Aug 2026, tested on one machine Author documents progressive audio degradation down a chain (lossy re-encode each hop) and a ~10ms constant audio offset Use instead: Seedance 2.5 30s single takes (fewer joins); API chaining with last frame -> next start image; one continuous VoiceStudio voice track and music added in ffmpeg assembly Trade-off the owner chose: chunks are individually editable; the cost is join artefacts (motion/audio continuity), which this node and last-frame chaining exist to reduce

items.name: HyperFrames
items.description: Open-source renderer: a video is an HTML file with timing attributes; animations from GSAP, CSS, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js or WAAPI are seeked frame by frame in headless Chrome and encoded with ffmpeg (npm package v0.8.143). Commands: init, preview, check, render (mp4, webm, mov with alpha, gif, png-sequence, hls), plus lint, snapshot, doctor, cloud render and Lambda render. Init can transcribe an audio file with whisper. Project ships AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md so an agent knows how to author. 5,399 commits, 5.3k forks.
items.verdictNote: ADOPT as the renderer for content studio explainers. Pilot on an 8 GB GPU before anything else is built on it.
items.why: RAN HERE: scaffold plus a 10-second 1920x1080 30 fps H.264 render took 23 s in draft quality on this CPU-only sandbox (about 2.3 s of render per second of video); sandbox could not download its preferred chrome-headless-shell, so it fell back to screenshot capture, which it says is slower; I pointed it at an installed Chromium with HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH It refuses to render when its own check finds a correctness warning: the starter loads GSAP from a CDN, which this sandbox blocks, and the render failed until I vendored GSAP locally. Good safety behaviour, but vendor GSAP and fonts for any offline or locked-down machine Anonymous usage telemetry exists (project and render events, per-skill attribution). I set DO_NOT_TRACK and HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY but did NOT verify those names are honoured: check its docs before running on a work machine Needs Node 22+, ffmpeg; each render worker is a separate Chrome (about 256 MB RAM each); an 8 GB machine is fine for 1080p, long 4K renders untested HeyGen-hosted cloud rendering and a desktop Studio are offered; pricing not shown; the repo says no per-render fees or commercial thresholds for the framework itself Young release line (0.8.x): pin the version

items.name: TRELLIS.2
items.description: Image-to-3D model producing PBR GLB assets (base colour, roughness, metallic, opacity). Hosted on fal at $0.25 (512), $0.30 (1024), $0.35 (1536) per generation.
items.verdictNote: ADOPT via fal pay-per-use ($0.25-0.35 each). It is cheaper than the Hunyuan3D v3 route in image-blaster (about $0.675) and MIT with no territory limits. Run locally only after a 24 GB card.

extra.released: Wan 2.2 date not stated in source

items.name: LTX-2.3 / LTX-2.5
items.description: Lightricks open-weights audio+video model; 2.3 (Mar 2026) has Q4 GGUF ~10GB at 960x544; 2.5 (Aug 11 2026) is 22B with multi-shot, 4K HDR.
items.why: Native synced audio is a new format; 2.3 Q4 ~10GB so 8GB needs offload (unverified), 2.5 22B is likely too big for 8GB.

items.name: Veo 3.1 Lite / Fast / Standard
items.description: Google video with native audio. Official per-second: Lite $0.05 (720p)/$0.08 (1080p); Fast $0.10-0.12; Standard $0.40.
items.why: Veo 3.1 Lite at ~$0.40-0.64 per 8s clip with audio is the cheapest premium-quality API option for hero clips.

items.name: Sora 2 API
items.description: API reported to sunset Sept 24 2026 per sources.
items.why: Reported API shutdown 2026-09-24; do not build on it.

items.name: Kling 3.0 Turbo
items.description: Kling 3.0 Turbo official 720p rate ~CNY0.8/s (~$0.11); native audio; fal lists Kling 3 Pro $0.224-0.28/s.
items.why: About $0.55-1.10 per 5-10s clip; strong motion but Veo Lite is cheaper with audio.

items.name: Seedance 2.x
items.description: ByteDance token-billed video; ~CNY1 (~$0.14)/s approx at 1080p-class; Seedance Mini ~$0.022/s; fal-listed Seedance 2.0 Fast ~$0.09/s.
items.why: Cheap image-to-video for b-roll (~$0.2-1.4 per clip) but prices are approximations.

items.name: MiniMax-H3 (Hailuo)
items.description: Released 2026-07-31; $0.13/s, 2K, native stereo audio.
items.why: About $0.65-1.30 per 5-10s clip; newest Hailuo, worth a test vs Veo Lite.

items.name: Runway / Pika
items.description: Not priced in sources I fetched.
items.why: No pricing found; not needed given cheaper alternatives.

items.name: fal.ai
items.description: Aggregator: Veo 3.1 Fast ~$0.10/s, Std $0.20/s, Sora 2 Pro $0.30-0.50/s, Kling 3 Pro $0.224/s, FLUX.2 pro $0.03/MP, Seedream 4.5 $0.04, Nano Banana Pro $0.15, Eleven v3 $0.10/1k chars.
items.why: One key for video/image/TTS pay-as-you-go keeps spend inside the $100/mo budget.

items.name: FLUX.2 [klein] 4B
items.description: Unified gen+edit; 4B Apache-2.0 fits ~8GB, ~2.6GB at Q4 GGUF (community blog); 9B is non-commercial.
items.why: Already in stack; keep 4B (commercial-safe); do not use 9B for paid client work.

items.name: GPT Image 2
items.description: OpenAI; vendor blog rates it best for accurate text; ~$0.01-0.41/img depending on quality.
items.why: Use only for text-heavy thumbnails where local Flux fails; quality-tier pricing varies.

items.name: Seedream 4.5 / 5.0 Lite
items.description: ByteDance; praised for text; $0.04 (4.5 on fal) / $0.032 (5.0 Lite).
items.why: Cheap bulk variants with good text at ~$0.03-0.04.

items.name: Qwen-Image / Qwen-Image-Edit
items.description: Open text-rendering image model; I found no 2026 source for specifics or 8GB fit.
items.why: Unverified from this research; check GGUF 8GB fit before adopting.

items.name: Chatterbox / Chatterbox Turbo
items.description: Resemble open TTS with voice cloning; Turbo Dec 2025; license MIT per most sources.
items.why: Free voice cloning as an upgrade over Kokoro; check 8GB co-residence with ComfyUI.

items.name: Higgs Audio V2
items.description: ~5.8B open TTS rated high fidelity; reportedly needs data-center GPU.
items.why: Too large for 8GB; use only on rented GPU.

items.name: Kokoro
items.description: 82M Apache TTS, CPU-friendly; already in stack.
items.why: Keep as the zero-cost narration voice: 82M parameters, Apache-2.0 code and weights, 9 languages incl. Hindi; last commit 2025-08-06, so treat it as stable rather than actively developed.

items.name: ElevenLabs Eleven v3
items.description: ~$0.10 per 1k characters (v3), $0.05 Flash; leads long-form consistency; dubbing price not found.
items.why: About $0.10 per ~1 min narration; use sparingly for flagship shorts.

items.name: Suno (paid plans)
items.description: Paid tiers grant commercial rights; monthly download caps; Warner settlement means licensed models coming; no official public API confirmed in my sources.
items.why: No confirmed API and licensing in flux; ACE-Step is safer and free.

items.name: Udio
items.description: Downloads suspended platform-wide during licensed-platform build per sources.
items.why: Downloads suspended, unusable for publishing.

items.name: Stable Audio 3
items.description: Reported open weights, up to ~6 min (single source).
items.why: Single-source claim; check license and size.

items.name: InfiniteTalk (open) / hosted
items.description: Audio-driven talking video; hosted $0.015/s 480p, $0.06/s 720p via Kie.ai. Local 8GB fit unverified.
items.why: About $0.15-0.60 per 10s hosted; local fit unknown on 8GB.

items.name: LatentSync (ByteDance)
items.description: Free open lip-sync on own GPU.
items.why: $0 lip-sync for dubbed shorts; VRAM need not verified.

items.name: HeyGen API
items.description: API needs min $100/mo plan, ~$0.10/s per third-party claim.
items.why: Plan minimum alone consumes the whole budget.

items.name: YouTube Test & Compare
items.description: Native YouTube Studio A/B testing of thumbnails (and titles per secondary sources). Official help says not available for Shorts.
items.why: Native and UI-only; we can only mimic via manual swaps, so surface a 'run test in Studio' reminder in the approval queue.

keyFeatures: Not for Shorts per official help

items.name: X API pay-per-use
items.description: Since 2026-02-06 pay-per-use is default for new X developers; reported $0.015/post create, $0.20 with URL, $0.005/post read. Legacy Basic/Pro closed to new signups.
items.why: Our live X publishing and inbox polling now cost per call; add a cost meter and avoid URL-in-post and heavy read polling. Prices from third-party guides, confirm in X console.

items.name: TikTok Content Posting API
items.description: Direct Post needs video.publish scope; unaudited clients are limited to private viewing. Upload (video.upload) sends drafts to creator inbox.
items.why: Ship TikTok first via Upload-to-inbox (fits our human approval queue) while the audit is pending.

extra.pricing: Free; audit takes ~1-2 weeks per third-party guide https://bundle.social/blog/tiktok-api-approval

items.name: Instagram Trial Reels via publishing API
items.description: Vendors claim trial Reel publishing now works through the official API (graduationStrategy param per Ayrshare docs); not confirmed in Meta docs.
items.why: Trial Reels are a free hook-test loop for solo creators; verify the param in Meta docs before building.

items.name: Threads API 2026 update
items.description: Reply approvals, publish/delete webhooks, 10,000-char text attachments, ghost posts, spoilers, GIPHY GIFs, keyword search, tokenless oEmbed, share to IG Stories.
items.why: Threads is a stub today and the API is now rich enough (webhooks + reply moderation) to feed the unified inbox.

items.name: Beehiiv
items.description: 2026: metered paywalls, paid trials, webinars (Apr); Summer release (Jul 16) adds AI copilot, community, podcast hosting, digital products, AI website builder.
items.why: Shows creators expect newsletter + monetization bundled; a newsletter-syndication step is the cheap match.

items.name: HeyGen Avatar V
items.description: Apr 8 2026 Avatar V model announced; Apr 7 Seedance 2.0 integration listed on the blog index.
items.why: Benchmark for avatar/UGC-style ads; we generate locally so only watch.

items.name: Mirage (Captions)
items.description: Captions rebranded Mirage, $75M raise Mar 2026; accent-preserving dubbing audio model; Co-Editor mode (Aug 2025). Secondary source only.
items.why: Accent-preserving multi-language dubbing is the bar for our voice pipeline.

items.name: vidIQ
items.description: Per secondary sources: AI Coach, daily AI video ideas with keyword/competition data, AI thumbnail/title generation.
items.why: Daily personalized ideas is the pattern to copy into the Brain + calendar.

items.name: Spotter Studio
items.description: AI ideation, titles, and personalized thumbnails from similar-creator analysis (2024 launch; no 2026 news found).
items.why: Packaging-first ideation workflow model.

items.name: Metricool
items.description: Vendor page lists SmartLinks 2.0, AI assistant, TikTok Music as 2026 features.
items.why: Link-in-bio plus analytics in one scheduler is table stakes.

items.name: OpenCreator (formerly KrillinAI)
items.description: Desktop creator workspace (macOS, Windows) driven by Codex CLI: video download and translation, image/video/voice generation, writing tools and agent chat; providers include OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, Gemini, Kling, Seedance, MiniMax and Edge TTS; local transcription via faster-whisper/whisper.cpp; data kept locally in SQLite. Optional paid account with credits via Stripe. Last commit 2026-10-16.
items.verdictNote: conditional: only for video translation/dubbing
items.why: Its KrillinAI roots (subtitle translation and dubbing) are the useful part; as a full workspace it is Codex/OpenAI-centred and duplicates a Claude-based pipeline. Many look-alike forks exist: use krillinai/OpenCreator only. Edge TTS is an unofficial Microsoft route with commercial-use doubts.

items.name: Short Video Factory
items.description: Cross-platform desktop app (v1.3.0, 2026-10-16) that turns a prompt plus your footage clips into batches of product-marketing short videos: AI copy via any OpenAI-compatible API, voiceover, auto editing, subtitles, effects. Chinese and English UI.
items.verdictNote: skip for now
items.why: Voice is Edge TTS only (unofficial Microsoft route; commercial use questionable), built for e-commerce product clips, and duplicates an HTML/ffmpeg or HyperFrames pipeline. AGPL is fine for desktop use.

items.name: Podcastfy
items.description: Turns URLs, PDFs, text or images into two-host podcast conversations in many languages; transcripts from 100+ LLMs (local supported); TTS via OpenAI, Google, ElevenLabs or Edge. Python 3.11+, ffmpeg. Last commit 2026-05-04 (README only).
items.verdictNote: assess: idea good, project slowing
items.why: No local TTS out of the box, so every episode costs TTS fees unless you patch in a local voice; recent commits are README updates only. Worth a test only if an audio-podcast channel is planned.

items.name: Social Media Agent (LangChain)
items.description: LangGraph agent: URL in, X and LinkedIn post drafts out, reviewed in an Agent Inbox (approve/edit/reject) and scheduled. Needs Anthropic API, FireCrawl, Arcade, LangSmith; full setup adds Vertex AI, X/LinkedIn developer apps, GitHub token, Supabase, Slack. Maintained (fix 2026-10-12).
items.verdictNote: reference: copy the review pattern
items.why: Six-plus services and keys for something an n8n flow plus a scheduler like Postiz already does; the human-in-the-loop Agent Inbox is the idea worth copying. X API posting has its own costs.

items.name: Poly Haven
items.description: Free HDRIs, PBR textures and 3D models, all CC0: commercial use, no attribution, redistribution allowed. blender-mcp can pull Poly Haven assets directly into Blender.
items.why: Best zero-risk source for lighting, surfaces and props. CC0 covers the assets only (logos, renders and site text are not CC0), and the Terms of Service forbid scraping or data mining without permission, so download normally rather than bulk-harvesting.

items.name: ambientCG
items.description: 2,000+ PBR materials, HDRIs, decals, atlases, terrains and some models under CC0 1.0 Universal; commercial use without permission or credit.
items.why: Complements Poly Haven for realistic surfaces; CC0 with no attribution needed. Supporter tiers exist on Patreon/Ko-fi but assets stay free.

items.name: Quaternius
items.description: Low-poly characters, props, environment mega-kits and retargetable humanoid animation libraries (Universal Animation Library 1 and 2), well suited to lightweight web games.
items.why: Licence is the Quaternius Asset License v1.0, NOT CC0 as often claimed: royalty-free in commercial games, no credit needed, but you may not sell or redistribute the assets themselves (even modified), so never commit raw packs to a public repo. Some packs sit behind Patreon; check each pack's licence.

items.name: Mixamo
items.description: Adobe's free auto-rigger and animation library: upload a humanoid character, get a rig and apply animations in one click; FBX export.
items.why: Free with an Adobe ID and royalty-free for personal, commercial and non-profit projects including video games (Adobe FAQ). Not available to Enterprise/Federated IDs or China accounts. The FAQ (last updated 2021) does not cover redistributing raw files or AI training: use it to animate characters, never as model-training data. Humanoids only.

items.name: Babylon.js
items.description: Full browser 3D game engine in TypeScript (scenes, physics, GUI, WebXR) with an online Playground, glTF Sandbox and shader tools. v9.17.0 tagged 2026-07-16.
items.why: More complete game engine than three.js (which is mainly a renderer). Worth it only if a 3D browser game outgrows a custom engine or three.js; pick one 3D stack per game rather than mixing.

items.name: Godot Engine
items.description: Free, open-source 2D/3D game engine under MIT; no royalties or fees; one-click export including web. Agent bridges: godot-ai and godot-mcp (see mcp-servers).
items.why: Already part of the toolset for side projects and prototypes; MIT means no revenue share. Check web-export size and browser support per project (not verified here).

items.name: comic-maker (Aillex)
items.description: One sentence to a lettered comic, fully local: Ollama writes the script (characters with locked looks, pages, panels, dialogue, SFX), ComfyUI renders each panel (Z-Image Turbo by default; swappable in ~30 lines), a PIL compositor adds layouts of 1-9 panels, speech bubbles, SFX, title strip and CBZ export. Styles: sunday-strip, manga, noir, euro-album. Last commit 2026-07-20.
items.verdictNote: trial first: best fit for a local Ollama + ComfyUI stack
items.why: No cloud, no credits, MIT, stages runnable separately with a hand-editable script.json. Early cut (7 files) and consistency relies on seeds plus restated looks, not a trained character model. VRAM of the default Z-Image Turbo checkpoint not checked; swap in an 8 GB-friendly model if needed.
items.source: research 2026-10-19: AI comics and cinematic references

items.name: StoryDiffusion
items.description: Consistent Self-Attention for keeping characters the same across panels with SD1.5/SDXL models, plus a motion predictor for longer videos. Last commit 2024-09-26.
items.verdictNote: catalogue for the 24 GB upgrade
items.why: The README's own low-VRAM script was tested on a 24 GB GPU and is expected to need more than 20 GB, so it does not fit 8 GB. Code is Apache-2.0; base-model licences (SDXL) apply. No updates since Sept 2024. On 8 GB, get consistency from character LoRAs or reference adapters in ComfyUI instead.
items.source: research 2026-10-19: AI comics and cinematic references

items.name: MangaNinja
items.description: CVPR 2025 line-art colorization that follows a colored reference image (keeps clothing and hair colors consistent) with point-click guidance. Community Windows port reports about 6 GB VRAM. Last commit 2025-03-02. Note the repo name is spelled MangaNinjia.
items.verdictNote: skip for anything sold
items.why: Licensed Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0: cannot be used for commercial comics. Fine for private experiments only.
items.source: research 2026-10-19: AI comics and cinematic references

items.name: AI Comic Factory
items.description: Story description plus art style to comic pages; LLM via Hugging Face, OpenAI, Groq or Anthropic; images via Hugging Face, Replicate or OpenAI.
items.verdictNote: skip: archived
items.why: Archived by its owner on 2025-10-31 (read-only). Every page needs paid cloud LLM and image providers; no fully local mode.
items.source: research 2026-10-19: AI comics and cinematic references

items.name: AI-Comic-Generator (Dapeng960208)
items.description: Vue + FastAPI manga tool: story to JSON storyboard, character extraction with three-view character sheets used as image references, single-panel redraw, batch drawing. Google Gemini only (gemini-3-flash-preview text, gemini-3-pro-image-preview images). Last commit 2026-01-28.
items.verdictNote: reference: copy the three-view character sheet idea
items.why: Locked to paid Gemini image calls, 12 stars, 20 commits. The useful pattern: generate a three-view sheet per character first and feed it as the reference for every panel.
items.source: research 2026-10-19: AI comics and cinematic references

items.name: ComicCrafter AI (Balajee2k)
items.description: Streamlit app: story to comic with session memory and targeted single-panel edits (image or dialogue) that keep other panels; curated styles; PNG/PDF export. Uses Google Gemini plus the paid ClipDrop image API. Last commit 2026-05-06.
items.verdictNote: reference: copy targeted panel edits
items.why: Paid APIs, and the MIT badge has no LICENSE file behind it, so reuse rights are unclear. One preset imitates the Tintin look: avoid styles named after real franchises.
items.source: research 2026-10-19: AI comics and cinematic references

items.name: Comic_Studio (CallmeTruong)
items.description: LangGraph comic agent: plans story, storyboard and dialogue with an OpenAI-compatible model, renders panels with a local SD 1.5 checkpoint, then a vision model checks each page for missing characters, props, actions and dialogue mismatches and re-renders up to 3 times; panels and bubbles editable individually. Last commit 2026-09-14.
items.verdictNote: reference: copy the vision-QA retry loop
items.why: No licence (all rights reserved by default) and 1 star, so don't reuse the code. Its default checkpoint is an adult-oriented SD 1.5 model; swap it. The inspect-then-regenerate loop is worth rebuilding in your own pipeline.
items.source: research 2026-10-19: AI comics and cinematic references

items.name: SHOT.CAFE
items.description: Searchable database of 24,321 film and commercial stills (187 films) with filters for shot size, angle, day/night, interior/exterior, colour, director and cinematographer; collections with a login.
items.verdictNote: step 1: find reference shots
items.why: Fastest way to find a reference frame by shot type. Stills belong to their studios and are shown for education: use them to describe a shot, never as image inputs for published work.
items.source: research 2026-10-19: AI comics and cinematic references

items.name: FILMGRAB
items.description: Galleries of film stills organised by director, cinematographer, production designer, genre and year (about 4,000 entries, estimated from page counts); Patreon-supported.
items.verdictNote: step 2: study composition and colour
items.why: Whole-film galleries show a consistent palette and framing language. Fair-dealing educational use only.
items.source: research 2026-10-19: AI comics and cinematic references

items.name: Eyecannndy
items.description: Free visual technique library (about 136 techniques, Aerial to Zoom) with example clips, run by Jacobi Mehringer and community-curated.
items.verdictNote: step 3: learn technique names
items.why: Gives the exact names for effects you see, which makes prompts precise. Self-described as never 100% accurate.
items.source: research 2026-10-19: AI comics and cinematic references

items.name: Melies cinematic techniques
items.description: 424 cinematic techniques (camera moves, framing, shot size, angles, lighting, composition, effects) with definitions, video examples and ready prompts on most, from the Melies AI video product.
items.verdictNote: step 4: technique to prompt
items.why: Most useful of the six: definitions plus prompts in one place, free. It sits inside a commercial AI-video product's site, so expect upsell.
items.source: research 2026-10-19: AI comics and cinematic references

items.name: AI Camera Movements
items.description: 46 camera movements in 7 categories with looping previews and one copyable prompt each, written for Kling, Seedance, Higgsfield and Runway.
items.verdictNote: step 5: camera move to prompt
items.why: Quick copy-paste camera prompts for the video models already in use. Its 'Turn into video' buttons are Higgsfield referral links.
items.source: research 2026-10-19: AI comics and cinematic references

items.name: GrokFilm
items.description: Cinema technique index of prompts and example reels for xAI's Grok Imagine (about 300 techniques claimed); Studio feature marked 'coming soon'. Run by TETSUO CORP, built by AgenC; no stated xAI affiliation.
items.verdictNote: optional step 6
items.why: Prompts are tuned for Grok Imagine, not the video models in use; counters were placeholders and pricing is not stated. Melies covers lighting and editing already.
items.source: research 2026-10-19: AI comics and cinematic references

items.name: TripoSR
items.description: Single image to 3D mesh in under 0.5 s on an A100; about 6 GB VRAM by default; vertex colours by default, optional baked texture. Last commit 2026-06-04.
items.verdictNote: trial: MIT fallback to Stable Fast 3D
items.why: Fits 8 GB. Stable Fast 3D is its successor with better UVs and textures, but SF3D needs Stability registration and visible 'Powered by Stability AI' credit; TripoSR is plain MIT with no such strings. Quality is prototype-grade: use for greybox props, then refine.

items.name: Drei
items.description: Ready-made helpers for React Three Fiber: camera controls, environments, skies, shadows, text, model loading and more. Last commit 2026-09-30.
items.verdictNote: adopt if the game or site is built on React Three Fiber
items.why: The standard companion to React Three Fiber; saves days of boilerplate. Only relevant if the stack is React; a plain three.js or custom engine gets nothing from it.

items.name: React Postprocessing
items.description: Post-processing effects for React Three Fiber (bloom, depth of field, noise, vignette and more), wrapping the postprocessing library. Last commit 2026-10-19.
items.verdictNote: conditional on a React Three Fiber stack
items.why: Biggest visual upgrade per line of code for R3F scenes; each effect costs GPU time, so test on phones before shipping.
